exercises.prompt: With the program's prices (grade A 410, grade B 330, grade C 200 francs per kilogram), how many francs does `Payments.Pay` return for a delivery of 12.5 kg of grade B?
hints: Multiply the weight by the grade's price, then round to whole francs.
exercises.solution: 12.5 × 330 = 4125 exactly, so rounding changes nothing: **4125** francs. (A test program printed `4125` for `Math.Round(12.5D * 330D, 0, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`.)

exercises.prompt:
What does this print?

```vb
Console.WriteLine($"{Math.Round(1234.5D)} {Math.Round(1234.5D, 0, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)}")
```

feedback.message: Not yet: `Math.Round` without a rounding mode sends halves to the even neighbour.
Not yet: `AwayFromZero` rounds 0.5 up for positive numbers.

hints: The default midpoint rule is "to even"; 1234 is even.
exercises.solution: By default `Math.Round` rounds a half to the nearest even number, giving 1234; `MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero` gives 1235. Output: **`1234 1235`**. The program names its rounding rule explicitly because people expect the second behaviour for money.

exercises.prompt: The export contains the line `2026-11-07,Uwimana,0,A`. What happens to it?

options.label: The `Delivery` constructor throws, `ReadAll` catches the `ArgumentException`, and a problem `0 kg is outside 0 to 500 kg (Parameter 'kilograms')` is reported
options.feedback: Yes. Every `TryParse` succeeds, so the record reaches the constructor, whose guard rejects a weight of zero.

options.label: It is paid 0 francs and appears in Uwimana's statement
options.feedback: Not yet: the constructor requires a weight greater than 0, so no `Delivery` is created.

options.label: The program stops with an unhandled exception
options.feedback: Not yet: `ReadAll` catches `ArgumentException` around the constructor and turns it into an `InputProblem`.

hints: Which checks does the line pass, and which one fails?
exercises.solution: The date, weight and grade all parse, so the record reaches `New Delivery(...)`, which throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` because `kilograms <= 0D`. That is an `ArgumentException`, so `ReadAll` records **an `InputProblem` with the message `0 kg is outside 0 to 500 kg (Parameter 'kilograms')`** and carries on.

exercises.prompt: Why does the reader check `[Enum].IsDefined(quality)` after `[Enum].TryParse` succeeds?

options.label: Because `TryParse` also accepts numbers: for the text `7` it returned `True` with a `Grade` value of 7, which is not A, B or C
options.feedback: Yes. A test printed `True 7 False` for `TryParse("7", ...)`, the parsed value, and `IsDefined`.

options.label: Because `TryParse` is case-sensitive and `IsDefined` is not
options.feedback: Not yet: the call passes `ignoreCase:=True`, which is why `b` was accepted.

options.label: It is not needed; it is there for documentation
options.feedback: Not yet: without it, a record with grade `7` would reach `PricePerKg(d.Quality)` and throw a `KeyNotFoundException`.

exercises.solution: An `Enum` is an integer with names. `[Enum].TryParse` accepts names and **numbers**, so `7` parses to a `Grade` with value 7, which has no name and no price. `IsDefined` rejects it; without the check the payment lookup would fail later, far from the cause.

feedback.message: Not yet: a dictionary created without a comparer compares string keys exactly, including case.
Not yet: the first dictionary was given `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`.

hints: Only one of the dictionaries was given a comparer.
exercises.solution: The first dictionary ignores case, so `m-014` matches `M-014`; the second uses the default, case-sensitive comparison. Output: **`True False`**. Visual Basic's own `=` on strings is case-sensitive too unless `Option Compare Text` is set, but collections never look at that option: they use their comparer.

exercises.prompt: Why does `DeliveryReader.ReadAll` take a `TextReader` rather than a file path?

options.label: So that the same code can read a file, a string or any other text source, which lets tests pass a `StringReader` without touching the disk
options.feedback: Yes. The xUnit theory feeds it one bad line at a time from a string.

options.label: Because `TextFieldParser` cannot open files by name
options.feedback: Not yet: `TextFieldParser` has a constructor that takes a path; the choice is about flexibility and testing.

options.label: Because reading from a `TextReader` is faster than reading a file
options.feedback: Not yet: a `StreamReader` over a file is itself a `TextReader`; speed is not the reason.

hints: Look at how the test class calls `ReadAll`.
exercises.solution: Accepting the general `TextReader` **decouples the parsing rules from where the text comes from**. The program passes a `StreamReader` over a file; the tests pass a `StringReader` over one line. This is the same idea as keeping input and output at the edge of the program.

exercises.prompt: After moving the classes into the `Coop.Core` library, the test project failed with *BC30002: Type 'Delivery' is not defined*, although it referenced the library. What fixed it?

options.label: Adding `Imports Coop.Core`, because a Visual Basic project places its code in the root namespace set in its project file
options.feedback: Yes. The library's `<RootNamespace>` is `Coop.Core`, so its types are `Coop.Core.Delivery` and so on.

options.label: Making the classes `Friend` instead of `Public`
options.feedback: Not yet: `Friend` would hide them from other assemblies altogether.

options.label: Turning `Option Strict` off in the test project
options.feedback: Not yet: the error is about names, not conversions.

hints: Where does a Visual Basic file's namespace come from when it has no `Namespace` block?
exercises.solution: Visual Basic projects wrap all their code in a **root namespace**, from `<RootNamespace>` in the project file. The library's types were therefore `Coop.Core.Delivery`, `Coop.Core.Payments` and so on, and **`Imports Coop.Core`** made them visible to the tests.
